rootCauseHypothesis:
The hosting-side invoice implementation likely does not provide a separate discount property in the invoice summary, either because the backend never computes/returns it or the frontend does not render it. Instead, the adjustment is encoded only as a negative line item (‘Advance paid at connection’), so the test cannot assert Taxable Amount == Subtotal - Discount because the required Discount field is absent. This indicates a mismatch between the invoice data model/UI and the expectations of the test. Underlying error: TEST BLOCKED

A required field needed for the test (a separate 'Discount' value) is not present on the invoice page, so the test cannot complete the requested assertions.

Observations:
- The invoice page shows Subtotal: ($110.00), Taxable amount: ($110.00), Service Tax (12.24%): ($13.46), and Total: ($123.46).
- No separate 'Discount' label or Discount value is visible on the invoice totals area; only a negative line-item (Advance paid at connection) appears in the line-items table, but there is no explicit Discount field to use for the assertion "Taxable Amount == Subtotal - Discount".

recommendedFixTarget.rationale: Update the invoice rendering/data contract so the totals section exposes a distinct Discount field whenever a discount/advance/credit is being applied, rather than only representing it as a negative line item. If the current business logic treats ‘Advance paid at connection’ as a discount-like adjustment, map it into an explicit discount amount in the invoice summary and ensure Taxable amount is calculated and displayed as Subtotal - Discount. Also verify the API/backend is sending the discount value to the frontend and the UI template includes it consistently for the relevant invoice type.
